tagline: Through a logging tunnel and into a gorge of arches.
intro: Out of Stanton the loop heads into the Daniel Boone National Forest and enters the gorge through Nada Tunnel, 900 feet of sandstone blasted out for a logging railroad in 1910 and 1911. The first trainload of logs stuck fast and had to be blasted free. The tunnel is a foot taller now and carries one lane of cars.

Beyond it the road winds under sandstone cliffs, with more than a hundred natural arches in the Red River Gorge Geological Area. The river nearly got a dam in the 1960s. A protest hike in 1967 brought out a Supreme Court justice, and in 1993 Wild and Scenic status ruled the dam out.

moments.title: Nada Tunnel
moments.text: Narrow-gauge locomotives once hauled timber through here to a sawmill in Clay City. When the forests were cut, the tracks came out and a dirt road went in.

moments.title: Slade
moments.text: The post office closed in 2004, but the climbers still come, and a pizza place's campground for them has been called Camp 4 of the East.

moments.title: Natural Bridge
moments.text: Two miles south of Slade, a sandstone arch 78 feet long and 65 feet high, reached by an Original Trail laid out in the 1890s, when a railroad ran the place for tourists.

practical: Nada Tunnel on KY 77 carries a single lane of traffic.
